title: Label triage sandbox journal
content:
Purpose / context:
This is my working notebook for building the lightweight triage rules we can ship to contract labelers for the next 2 sprints. Aim: reduce reviewer overhead by ~30% on clear-cut cases while preserving recall on hard entity splits. Not a final spec — lots of 'notes to self' and quick examples.

High-level approach (starter):
- Create 3 buckets for incoming ambiguous rows: auto-resolve (heuristic safe), needs-review (human), reject-as-noise.
- Heuristics should be conservative: precision > 98% for auto-resolve. Anything uncertain goes to needs-review.
- Prioritize fixes that reduce reviewer time (common patterns, high volume).

Quick heuristics I'm testing (priority order):
1) Numeric-id-as-username: if token matches /^[A-Z]{2}-?\d{4,}$/ and context has no alphabetic full name, tag AS_ID.
2) Email-like tokens with obvious redaction (<user>@<redacted>.com) => mark CONTACT if domain present, else needs-review.
3) Short tokens with punctuation like "A.B." within a sentence: usually initials; if adjacent tokens contain last name, resolve as PERSON_INITIALS.
4) Long camelCase tokens > 20 chars => likely code artifact => tag CODE_ARTIFACT (auto-resolve).
5) URL fragments inside quoted fields without whitespace -> keep as URL if scheme present; if only path-like and context is dataset id -> needs-review.

Examples and edge cases I ran into:
- "JAX-0001" in policy text: matches numeric-id heuristic, auto-resolve AS_ID. But if there is a preceding "Project" and subsequent uppercase word = TEAM, then reconsider as PROJECT_CODE (needs new label). TODO: add project vs id disambiguation rule.
- "alex@redacted" -> no TLD; our current rule marks CONTACT only if domain contains ".". Decide: treat as CONTACT but tag SOURCE_UNKNOWN and route to reviewer. (Note: contractors often redact like this.)
- "Dr. S. K." within clinical notes -> initials frequently used for staff; if 'Dr.' present, auto-resolve PERSON (but flag for medical note privacy).

Labeling snippets (what to tell labelers):
- If it's a sequence of digits separated by dashes and appears in a form field, label as FORM_ID. Example: "123-45-678" -> FORM_ID.
- Dates: any token matching typical date regex (MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, Month name variants) tagged DATE; ambiguous short forms like "3/4" -> reviewer.
- PII vs. non-PII: if token is a short city name (e.g., "Paris") within general text, treat as NON-PII unless paired with street or postal details.

Operational triage flow (manual + heuristics):
1) Pass through regex heuristics.
2) For tokens flagged auto-resolve, run small QA sample: 200 random auto-resolve items per label type weekly; if error rate >2%, flip to needs-review.
3) Needs-review items go to labeler queue with contextual window = 120 chars on either side. Provide top-3 likely labels predicted by model to speed decision.
4) Reject-as-noise: preserve a small reservoir (1%) for spot checks to ensure we didn't lose rare true positives.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to handle multilingual names (accented characters) in regexes? We should use Unicode categories in production regexes; for sandbox, keep naive and add escalation when >0.5% FNs show up.
- Project-level label "PROJECT_CODE" vs "AS_ID" conflict — need dictionary-based override (maintain small list of known Project prefixes).
- Should we expose a 'context hint' boolean to labelers indicating high-sensitivity text (HIPAA/financial)? Feels necessary for extra reviewer caution.

Small experiment ideas to validate heuristics quickly:
- Run heuristic set vs gold subset (n=1k): measure precision and recall per label. If precision < 98% for auto-resolve set, tighten rules.
- A/B test two reviewer UIs: (A) show model suggestions only, (B) show model + top-3 similar examples. Measure time per decision.

Example labeled samples for training (copy-paste friendly):
1) "User: 0192-Alpha logged in at 2024-10-03." -> [0192-Alpha] = AS_ID (auto) ; [2024-10-03] = DATE (auto)
2) "Contact: support@acme.com (redacted)" -> [support@acme.com] = CONTACT (auto-resolve)
3) "Ref: PRJ-ECO-832 next steps" -> [PRJ-ECO-832] = needs-review (possible PROJECT_CODE)
4) "note: see /data/models/llamav2/big-run" -> [/data/models/...] = CODE_ARTIFACT (auto)

Reviewer notes (for contract labelers):
- If unsure, choose NEEDS_REVIEW. Don't invent labels.
- Keep span minimal (do not include trailing punctuation unless part of token).
- When tagging names, prefer full name spans when available; initials-only tags acceptable when no last name present.

Personal action items (me):
- Build a tiny regex lib (python) with these heuristics and a test harness (JIRA-3421).
- Draft a 1-pager for contractors explaining 'why' behind heuristics (for buy-in).
- Add a weekly QA check that samples auto-resolved labels per category.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Need to record examples where auto-resolve fails: file at /tmp/auto-resolve-failures-2025-02-14.csv
- Think about incorporating light ML classifier for borderline cases rather than expanding rules too far — rules should handle high-volume easy cases only.

End of page. Quick raw thought: the label taxonomy needs a compact 'meta' flag for 'sensitive' that we can attach to spans so downstream can apply stricter handling.
short_summary: Working journal for building conservative triage heuristics to auto-resolve common label patterns and route ambiguous examples to human reviewers; includes heuristics, examples, flow, and TODOs.
